cve_summary: fs/overlayfs/copy_up.c in the Linux kernel before 4.2.6 uses an incorrect cleanup code path, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (dentry reference leak) via filesystem operations on a large file in a lower overlayfs layer.
commit_message:
ovl: fix dentry reference leak

In ovl_copy_up_locked(), newdentry is leaked if the function exits through
out_cleanup as this just to out after calling ovl_cleanup() - which doesn't
actually release the ref on newdentry.

The out_cleanup segment should instead exit through out2 as certainly
newdentry leaks - and possibly upper does also, though this isn't caught
given the catch of newdentry.

Without this fix, something like the following is seen:

	BUG: Dentry ffff880023e9eb20{i=f861,n=#ffff880023e82d90} still in use (1) [unmount of tmpfs tmpfs]
	BUG: Dentry ffff880023ece640{i=0,n=bigfile}  still in use (1) [unmount of tmpfs tmpfs]

when unmounting the upper layer after an error occurred in copyup.

An error can be induced by creating a big file in a lower layer with
something like:

	dd if=/dev/zero of=/lower/a/bigfile bs=65536 count=1 seek=$((0xf000))

to create a large file (4.1G).  Overlay an upper layer that is too small
(on tmpfs might do) and then induce a copy up by opening it writably.

Signed-off-by: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Miklos Szeredi <miklos@szeredi.hu>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # v3.18+
docstring:
"""
Summary: 
Copies up a single dentry in an overlay filesystem, handling directory renames and ensuring proper permissions.

Parameters:
parent (struct dentry *): The parent directory of the dentry to copy up.
dentry (struct dentry *): The dentry to be copied up.
lowerpath (struct path *): The path of the lower filesystem.
stat (struct kstat *): The status information of the dentry.
attr (struct iattr *): Attributes to set on the dentry after copying up.

Returns:
int: Returns 0 on success, or a negative error code on failure.

Logic:
The function first checks for the existence of a work directory. It retrieves the attributes of the parent directory and handles symbolic links if necessary. It prepares credentials for the operation, raising necessary capabilities. The function locks the directories involved to prevent race conditions during the copy-up process. If the upper dentry already exists, it updates its attributes if provided. If not, it performs the copy-up operation and restores timestamps on the parent directory. Finally, it cleans up resources and returns the result of the operation.
"""
